headline: KSE-100 falls for a second day to 172,642 as an unresolved US-Iran conflict, a widening US-Canada trade war and a coin-flip Fed decision weigh on sentiment
mood: Risk premiums widen · Fed decision now a coin flip, trade war escalates

five_things.html: The benchmark eased 993.92 points (0.57%) to close at 172,642.16 on Tuesday, retreating from an intraday high of 173,736.19 to a low of 171,490.63 as selling persisted for a second straight session. Volume rose to 722.62 million shares worth Rs27.94bn, though breadth stayed decisively negative at 101 advancers to 359 decliners (36 unchanged) out of 496 traded names. UBL, LUCK, MEBL, NBP and PPL dragged the index down roughly 485 points; PSEL, MCB and ATRL offset with about 199 points combined. Topline Securities said the bourse “came under pressure today as the ongoing US-Iran conflict and elevated international oil prices continued to weigh on investor sentiment.” Sources: Business Recorder, The Express Tribune.

Brent settled near $97.4/bbl (+0.26%) and WTI topped $94/bbl intraday before paring to around $92.8/bbl, both holding near three-month highs as the ongoing US-Iran conflict keeps traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — which historically carried roughly 20% of global oil trade — severely restricted. OPEC+'s seven core members (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, following the UAE's May exit from the group) held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting. Sources: Trading Economics, Gulf News.

Canada's counter-tariffs on roughly $20–27.6bn of US goods — spanning steel, aluminium (duties doubled to 50%), dairy, appliances, agri-equipment and pulp and paper — took effect Tuesday, matching Washington's levies dollar-for-dollar. The Trump administration responded with fresh import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages due 29 September, adding a second macro headwind alongside firmer oil to Tuesday's US equity slide. Sources: Al Jazeera, Canada.ca.

five_things.chip: Fed Decision Now A Coin Flip
five_things.html: CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp hike at the 16 September FOMC have eased to roughly 50–56% from 58–60% shortly after Jackson Hole, with Kalshi (48%) and Polymarket (49%) also pricing a near coin-flip outcome. The 10-year Treasury briefly ticked back above 4.8% on Tuesday before settling near 4.79%, with the 2-year flat at 4.38%, as traders weighed Chair Warsh's hawkish tone against fiscal-risk concerns flagged by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Sources: CNBC, CNBC.

five_things.chip: IMF Mission Homes In On SWF Bill
five_things.html: Pakistan's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026, tabled in the Senate and referred to its Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, is expected to be a focus of the IMF's fourth EFF and third RSF review mission due in Islamabad this month; the bill adds fiscal safeguards, tightens governance and expands disclosure requirements for SWF-held state enterprises. It lands against a backdrop of August CPI at 11.1% y/y, an SBP policy rate held at 11.5% and 6-month KIBOR at 11.86%. Sources: Business Recorder, ProPakistani.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape extended its slide for a second session: the KSE-100 fell 993.92 points (0.57%) to close at 172,642.16 on Tuesday, having shed almost 2,700 points over two sessions as the ongoing US-Iran conflict and a firmer oil tape unsettled investors. Breadth stayed negative at 101 advancers to 359 decliners out of 496 names, with UBL, LUCK, MEBL, NBP and PPL the heaviest drags (~485 points) against a partial offset from PSEL, MCB and ATRL (~199 points); volume rose to 722.62 million shares worth Rs27.94bn. On policy, the government's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, a governance overhaul the IMF is expected to scrutinise when its fourth EFF/third RSF review mission arrives this month. August CPI held at 11.1% y/y, the SBP's policy rate stays at 11.5%, 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.86%, and USD/PKR interbank was little changed near 277.37. Sources: Business Recorder, Business Recorder.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf oil benchmarks held near three-month highs as the US-Iran conflict kept traffic through the Strait of Hormuz severely restricted: Brent settled around $97.4/bbl and WTI near $92.8/bbl after topping $94 intraday. OPEC+'s seven core producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, following the UAE's exit from the group in May — held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting, continuing the existing roadmap into year-end. Saudi's PIF, meanwhile, is executing its board-approved 2026–2030 strategy, having launched the Gulf Coast Development Company on 7 September to build an integrated coastal destination at Al-Khafji, part of a broader push into tourism, urban development and clean energy under Vision 2030. Sources: Gulf News, PIF.
matrix.global_html: US equities fell for a second straight session Tuesday as a firmer oil tape and an escalating US-Canada trade war outweighed any Fed relief: the S&P 500 slipped 0.58% to 7,673.52, the Dow dropped 1.18% (over 600 points) to 52,786.07 and the Nasdaq eased 0.32% to 26,421.41. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20–27.6bn of US goods took effect the same day, and Washington answered with fresh import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcohol from 29 September. The 10-year Treasury briefly topped 4.8% before settling near 4.79%, with the 2-year flat at 4.38%, as fiscal-risk concerns flagged by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added to hawkish-Fed positioning ahead of the 16 September FOMC, where CME FedWatch now prices roughly a 50–56% hike probability. Gold eased to $4,394/oz and silver held near $65.7/oz. Sources: CNBC, CNBC.

legislative.policy_html: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — tabled in the Senate and referred to its Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, tightening SWF governance, fiscal safeguards and disclosure ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission.
legislative.sectors: State-owned enterprises, sovereign fund-held assets, banks
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Investors and IMF stakeholders gain clearer governance and disclosure standards, potentially easing the path to the next EFF/RSF tranche release. Loses: SWF-held state enterprises face tighter accountability and reporting obligations, raising near-term compliance costs.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+'s seven core members held October production quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting, continuing the existing roadmap into year-end as Brent holds near three-month highs.
legislative.sectors: Oil & gas majors, Gulf shipping/insurance, non-oil private sector
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Producers retaining current quotas amid a firm oil tape near $97/bbl, and Saudi's PIF-backed diversification projects such as the Gulf Coast Development Company. Loses: Gulf shippers, insurers and energy importers exposed to a persistent Hormuz risk premium.

legislative.policy_html: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20–27.6bn of US goods took effect 8 September, doubling steel and aluminium duties to 50% and hitting dairy, appliances and pulp and paper.
legislative.sectors: US & Canadian steel, aluminium, dairy, agri-equipment, autos
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Non-US/Canada steel and aluminium exporters gaining relative price competitiveness. Loses: US exporters facing the new Canadian tariffs, and US consumers — studies suggest importers absorb the bulk of tariff costs — ahead of Washington's own import bans on Canadian goods from 29 September.

levels.support_note: Tuesday's intraday low (171,491); deeper support at 170,000

desk_stance_html: Tuesday's 485-point drag from UBL, LUCK, MEBL, NBP and PPL against a thin 199-point offset from PSEL, MCB and ATRL, alongside breadth of 101 advancers to 359 decliners and rising volume (722.62m shares vs 679.19m Monday), suggests the two-day, nearly 2,700-point slide reflects sustained distribution rather than a one-off shock. The proximate triggers — an unresolved US-Iran conflict keeping Brent near $97.4/bbl, a widening US-Canada trade war, and a finely balanced 16 September FOMC (hike odds near 50–56%) — are unlikely to clear before the Fed decision. We'd stay defensive on broader beta into the FOMC while retaining selective exposure to banks and E&P names that benefit from a firmer oil tape, alongside SWF-adjacent names positioned to benefit from tighter governance ahead of the IMF's review mission. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 993.92 points (0.57%) to close at 172,642.16 on Tuesday, extending its slide to almost 2,700 points over two sessions as the ongoing US-Iran conflict and firmer oil prices unsettled investors. Breadth stayed negative at 101 advancers to 359 decliners out of 496 names, with UBL, LUCK, MEBL, NBP and PPL the heaviest drags (~485 points) against a partial offset from PSEL, MCB and ATRL (~199 points); volume rose to 722.62 million shares worth Rs27.94bn. On policy, the government's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, a governance overhaul the IMF is expected to scrutinise during its fourth EFF/third RSF review mission this month. August CPI held at 11.1% y/y, the SBP's policy rate stays at 11.5%, 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.86%, and USD/PKR interbank held near 277.37.

GCC
Gulf oil benchmarks held near three-month highs as the conflict kept traffic through the Strait of Hormuz severely restricted. OPEC+'s seven core producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, following the UAE's exit from the group in May — held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting. Saudi's PIF is executing its board-approved 2026–2030 strategy, having launched the Gulf Coast Development Company on 7 September to build an integrated coastal destination at Al-Khafji, part of a broader Vision 2030 push into tourism, urban development and clean energy.

GLOBAL
Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20–27.6bn of US goods — spanning steel, aluminium (duties doubled to 50%), dairy, appliances and pulp and paper — took effect Tuesday, matching Washington's levies dollar-for-dollar; the Trump administration answered with fresh import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcohol from 29 September. CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp hike at the 16 September FOMC have eased to roughly 50–56%, with Kalshi and Polymarket both pricing a near coin-flip outcome, as traders weigh Chair Warsh's hawkish tone against fiscal-risk concerns flagged by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: The Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, tightening governance ahead of the IMF's review mission.
• GCC: OPEC+ held October quotas steady at its 6 September meeting, continuing its roadmap into year-end.
• Global: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20–27.6bn of US goods took effect 8 September, doubling steel and aluminium duties to 50%.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 — Support 171,500 (deeper support 170,000) · Pivot 172,642 (Tuesday's close) · Resistance 173,740 (Tuesday's intraday high, then 175,350).

Desk stance: Tuesday's heavy-cap drag from UBL, LUCK, MEBL, NBP and PPL against a thin offsetting gain, rising volume and a roughly 3.5-to-1 negative breadth ratio suggest the two-day, nearly 2,700-point slide reflects sustained distribution. The proximate triggers — an unresolved US-Iran conflict, a widening US-Canada trade war, and a finely balanced FOMC — are unlikely to clear before 16 September. We'd stay defensive on broader beta into the decision while retaining selective exposure to banks and E&P names that benefit from firmer oil, alongside SWF-adjacent names positioned to benefit from tighter governance.
